topic: MiCA Article 68 CASP authorization — transitional deadline 1 July 2026
corrected_from: 2026-07-03 version cited Article 23 (wrong — that's the crypto-asset issuance article, not CASP authorization) and December 2024 as deadline (wrong — transitional window was 1 July 2026 under Article 143(3))
body:
The MiCA transitional deadline for crypto-asset service providers passed on 1 July 2026.

Here's what that actually means — and what happens next.

MiCA Article 68 requires every CASP (exchange, custodian, portfolio manager, transfer agent) to obtain authorization from the national competent authority (NCA) of its home member state before providing services.

Article 143(3) gave existing CASPs — those operating under national frameworks before 30 December 2024 — an 18-month window to apply. That window closed 1 July 2026.

**The NCA picture right now:**

BaFin (Germany): strict completeness gate — the 25 working-day clock under Article 62(4) only starts once the full package is submitted. Many applications are sitting in incompleteness loops.

AMF (France): existing DASP registrants have a streamlined conversion path — faster for those who registered early under the national regime.

CBI (Ireland): historically accessible for EU fintech licensing. Several CASP applications acknowledged before July 1 are proceeding under Article 143(3) protection.

**If you're in limbo:**

If your application was submitted and acknowledged as pending before 1 July 2026, most NCAs have confirmed you can continue operating while it processes. Document your submission date and NCA acknowledgment carefully.

If you missed the deadline entirely — you're in breach of Article 59. Fines under Article 120 can reach €5M or 3% of annual turnover.

The ESMA technical standards (ESMA/2024/1710 and /1711) specify the exact format NCAs expect. Non-conforming applications trigger an incompleteness finding that resets the 25-day completeness clock.
